- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with volatility decay.  
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price range in early 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to lower bound and 0.5–1.0% to upper bound for improved range accuracy.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to forecast if recent 7-day average is above 30-day average.
